newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn continues to press Iran over journalist.
newsitem.headline: Bonn continues to press Iran over journalist.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday Bonn was doing its utmost to investigate the case of an Iranian editor arrested for allegedly trying to leave Iran illegally, and rejected Tehran's charge of interference.

Kinkel told German Radio he had written two letters to Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati concerning Faraj Sarkuhi, editor of the Iranian monthly magazine Adineh (Friday). Sarkuhi's wife and children live in Germany.

Bonn wants Iran to provide details of Sarkuhi's whereabouts following reports he was not only detained earlier this month but also held and tortured by the Iranian secret service in Tehran late last year, when Iran insists he was in Germany.

"We're doing everything to clear up this case," Kinkel said. "I've sent two letters to Velayati. He said he wouldn't allow any interference. I told him this could not be classed as interference as Sarkuhi's wife and children are in Germany."
Kinkel said the European Union's "troika" of the current president -- the Netherlands -- and its immediate predecessor and successor was also pursuing the case.
"We've asked the Iranian ambassador into the Foreign Ministry several times and our ambassador has made our position clear. I can't really do anything more," he said.
In a letter published in several Western newspapers, Sarkuhi said the Iranian sercret service forced him into confessing in a taped interview that he was a spy for Germany.

He said in the letter, which Bonn believes is genuine, that he feared Tehran planned to use his confession as bargaining chip in a row with Germany over a Berlin murder trial. But Kinkel said he had no evidence to back up this theory.
"I can't convincingly make the connection at the moment," he said. "There's some speculation at the moment which I can't confirm."

Prosecutors have accused Tehran of ordering the 1992 killings of three Kurdish dissidents and their translators in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant. Iran has denied any involvement. An Iranian and four Lebanese are on trial for the shootings.

"I have always said that when the Mykonos trial comes to an end, it could make an evaluation of our relations with Iran necessary," Kinkel added. The trial verdict is expected within the next few months.
On Tuesday a group of opposition Social Democrat (SPD) members of parliament cancelled a visit to Iran planned for this weekend, after a meeting with the Iranian ambassador to Bonn.

The SPD declined to give reasons. But media reports said the decision not to go was linked to the fact that the delegation saw no prospect of progress in the Sarkuhi case and feared they might even make his situation worse.
